reasoning_summary: Verified both proofs step by step in order. Proof 1 Necessary (0004-0062): specializing full naturality of alpha on C x D to (f, id_D) and (id_C, g) yields the two squares, which under F(-,D)(f)=F(f,id_D), F(C,-)(g)=F(id_C,g) and alpha(C,-)_D = alpha(-,D)_C = alpha_{(C,D)} are exactly naturality of alpha(-,D) and alpha(C,-); justified. Proof 1 Sufficient (0066-0140): the alpha(-,D)-square at f and the alpha(C',-)-square at g (hypothesis (1) applied at object C') paste; bifunctoriality plus product-category composition give F(f,g)=F(id_{C'},g) o F(f,id_D) and likewise for G, so the outer rectangle is the naturality square for (f,g); justified. Proof 2 Necessary (0145-0203): (3) and (4) are valid instances of naturality, and both eqn chains are correct rewritings using the substitution definitions. Proof 2 Sufficient (0207-0251): main chain G(f,g)o alpha_{(C,D)} = G(id_{C'},g)oG(f,id_D)o alpha = G(id_{C'},g)o alpha_{(C',D)} o F(f,id_D) [by (3)] = alpha_{(C',D')} o F(id_{C'},g) o F(f,id_D) [by (4) at C'] = alpha_{(C',D')} o F(f,g); every hypothesis instance is at an object for which it is assumed. Only defects found are cosmetic transcription slips that no inference depends on: diagram edge labels at 0041 and 0080 print F where G is meant, line 0181 prints f where g is meant (the substituted term G(id_C,g) is correct), and line 0218 displays (3) with G on the right-hand side where F belongs while the correct form of (3) is the one actually used at 0236. No step is unjustified.
